# Battery optimisation report

*Generated by scripts/06_write_reports.py from the latest run (solver backend: pyomo).*

## Formulation

Per 15-minute interval *t* (Δt = 0.25 h): charge c_t ∈ [0, 100] kW, discharge d_t ∈ [0, 100] kW, SOC s_t ∈ [S_min,t, 450] kWh
(end of interval), grid import g_t ∈ [0, 600] kW.

    min  Σ_t g_t · Δt · p_t / 1000  +  0.015 · Σ_t (c_t + d_t) · Δt
    s.t. s_t = s_(t-1) + Δt · 0.975 · c_t − Δt · d_t / 0.975,   s_(-1) = 250 kWh
         g_t = L_t + c_t − d_t,  g_t ≥ 0                         (grid export is not possible)
         d_t − c_t ≤ L_low,t ;  L_high,t + c_t − d_t ≤ 600        (safety versions, strategy B)
         s_t ≥ 250 kWh at 23:45 every day (carried over midnight)

Implemented in Pyomo and solved with HiGHS (`src/optimization/battery.py`); the identical LP in SciPy-HiGHS is the
fallback and cross-check.

## LP, not MILP

"No simultaneous charge and discharge" would need binary variables, but it can never be optimal here: all prices are
positive, a round trip loses 5 %, and degradation is charged on both flows. The LP therefore satisfies it by itself,
verified on every run:

| Run | Solver | Total cost (EUR) | Simultaneous intervals |
|---|---|---|---|
| LP full month (strategy A) | pyomo/appsi_highs | 9,434.43 | 0 |
| LP rolling daily (strategy A) | pyomo/appsi_highs (rolling daily) | 9,435.44 | 0 |
| SciPy cross-check (strategy A) | scipy/highs-lp | 9,434.43 | 0 |

Full month is the main run; rolling daily (realistic, prices arrive day-ahead) costs almost the same because the daily
reserve separates the days.

Days with `forecast_available = 0` (2025-12-06, 2025-12-14, 2025-12-21): temperatures are imputed by the Forecasting
Service; the load model does not use temperature, so forecasts and schedules on those days are unaffected.

## Operational analysis

- **Charge** in the cheapest night quarter-hours and again 22:00–24:00 to meet the 250 kWh reserve (energy-weighted
  price 20.1 EUR/MWh).
- **Discharge** in the ~14 most expensive midday quarter-hours (79.8 EUR/MWh): 350 kWh usable energy at
  25 kWh per interval. Every day cycles fully; the daily spread (60–94 EUR/MWh) beats the ~30 EUR/MWh lost to efficiency
  and degradation.
- **Price periods that drive decisions:** the night/late-evening minimum and the midday maximum.
- **Forecast uncertainty** matters only where a constraint binds: the no-export limit during the shutdown, where the load
  (~35 kW) is below the discharge power. The 600 kW grid limit never binds in December.

## Recommendation

Deploy **strategy B**, run as a rolling daily optimisation. It costs only a few euros more per month than A, while A's
plan would push energy into the grid whenever the actual shutdown load is below its median forecast; grid export is not
allowed. Degradation takes roughly half of the gross arbitrage value, so the €0.015/kWh assumption matters as much as
forecast accuracy.
